newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: OECD criticises Slovak government bank selloff plans.
newsitem.headline: OECD criticises Slovak government bank selloff plans.

text.p: The Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD) on Monday criticised Slovakia's plans to privatise its leading financial institutions by selling stakes to domestic companies.

"We do not consider plans to privatise the four major financial institutions by large companies as good," Maitland MacFarlan, an OECD expert on central and eastern Europe, told a seminar in Bratislava.

The government has announced it will support banking sell-offs to large local companies, which are, in most cases the banks' major debtors. But the process has been postponed by law until the end of March next year.
Another OECD expert, Joaquin Oliviera Martins, told the seminar that such a method of privatisation would undermine the entire privatisation process.
He said that before privatisation could begin, the banks require a restructuring of their loan portfolios and an increase in their basic capital.
"Privatisation of Slovak banks by local companies would bring a clear risk to the process," Martins said.
"From the point of view of banks' equity increase, we do not see enough sources in Slovakia and this will require the participation of foreign capital," he added.

Privatisation of Slovakia's four major financial institutions -- commercial banks VUB and IRB, savings bank Slovenska Sporitelna and insurer Slovenska Poistovna -- is seen as crucial further restructuring of the economy and for its acceptance into the western economic structures.
Though the cabinet also welcomed foreign capital to participate in the banking privatisation, it had so far not made clear to what extent foreign subjects will be allowed to buy into the banks.

Finance Minister Sergej Kozlik in October said foreign participation in the privatisation of banks should be through an increase of their basic capital rather than through the purchase of existing shares.
